history.period: Ancient; claimed thousands of years old, possibly before the Mahabharata era (legendary - unverified)
history.summary: An ancient Shiva temple on the banks of the Sabarmati river at Randesan village near Gandhinagar, often called the 'Kashi of Gujarat' - devotees who cannot visit Kashi are said to earn equal merit by visiting here and bathing in the Sabarmati. Legend says Lord Indra bathed in the Sabarmati to absolve himself of Brahma Hatya (killing a Brahmin) and then built this temple, consecrating the Shivlinga - hence the alternate name Indreshwar Mahadev. Another local legend says a shepherd discovered a white Shivlinga here after noticing his cow giving milk at the spot; 'dhola' (white in Gujarati) gives the deity the name Dholeshwar. The temple's importance is said to be mentioned in Puranas of Maharshi Ved Vyas. The complex includes the main carved shrine, a yagya shala, gaushala, saint nivas and a garden. name: Shree Dholeshwar Mahadev Temple
town: Randesan (CSV town 'Gandhinagar' is the nearby city/district - the temple is in Randesan village, Gandhinagar)
town_description: Randesan is a village on the banks of the Sabarmati river on the north-western edge of Gandhinagar city, now effectively part of its urban sprawl. It is known chiefly for the ancient Dholeshwar Mahadev temple complex, with the river ghat, yagya shala and gaushala around it. Quiet and green compared to the city sectors, it draws steady Shiva devotees especially during Shravan.
